aspects.says: A Stream.Builder throws IllegalStateException on add after build().
basis: section:Builder and concat Assemble a Stream; Repeated concat Overflows the Stack
aspects.reason: the JDK's own check, with nothing for the reader to compute

aspects.says: String.chars() streams UTF-16 units, so a supplementary character counts twice and a cut can split it; codePoints() streams code points.
basis: section:String.chars() Streams UTF-16 Units, Not Characters

aspects.says: Repeated Stream.concat nests, and deep nesting overflows the stack (observed at 50,000 with the default stack); flatMap over a list of streams does not.
basis: section:Builder and concat Assemble a Stream; Repeated concat Overflows the Stack

aspects.says: A stream from Files.lines, Files.list or Files.walk keeps its file or directory open after the terminal operation, until close(); try-with-resources closes it even when reading fails.
basis: section:A Stream Over a File Holds It Open Until close(), Not Until the Terminal Operation

aspects.says: flatMap closes each inner stream after its elements pass, while closing a BufferedReader.lines() stream leaves the reader open.
basis: section:A Stream Over a File Holds It Open Until close(), Not Until the Terminal Operation
aspects.reason: both are JDK behaviours with nothing for the reader to compute; log-scan accepts a flatMap solution as well as a loop

aspects.says: A HashSet's (and Set.of's) stream has no encounter order: findFirst() follows the bucket layout, which a resize or, for Set.of, a JVM restart changes.
basis: section:A Collection's Stream Has the Collection's Order, and a HashSet Has None

aspects.says: IntStream.sum() returns an int and wraps silently; asLongStream().sum() or summaryStatistics().getSum() gives a long.
basis: section:Only Primitive Streams Have sum() and average(), and IntStream.sum() Overflows

aspects.says: The two-argument Stream.iterate is endless and a filter does not end it; the three-argument form stops when hasNext is false.
basis: section:A Generated Sequence Ends Only Where Its Factory Says

aspects.says: Unclosed file streams pile up descriptors until the process hits its limit, released only when a garbage collection happens to run.
basis: section:A Stream Over a File Holds It Open Until close(), Not Until the Terminal Operation

aspects.says: A Map is streamed through entrySet(), keySet() or values(), in the map's order.
basis: section:A Collection's Stream Has the Collection's Order, and a HashSet Has None
aspects.reason: choosing a view is a one-call idiom with nothing to decide; the order part is the HashSet question

aspects.says: Stream.of on an int[] is a stream of one element, the array; Arrays.stream or IntStream.of streams the values.
basis: section:Stream.of Streams Its Arguments: an int[] Is One Element, and So Is null

aspects.says: Stream.of(x) with x null holds one null, while Stream.ofNullable(x) is empty for null.
basis: section:Stream.of Streams Its Arguments: an int[] Is One Element, and So Is null

aspects.says: onClose handlers run when close() is called, not when the terminal operation ends.
basis: section:A Stream Over a File Holds It Open Until close(), Not Until the Terminal Operation
aspects.reason: the page shows it with a run; the log-scan practice relies on onClose to watch closing, and a separate graded task would only repeat that observation

aspects.says: sum(), average() and summaryStatistics() exist only on primitive streams; average() is an OptionalDouble, empty for no elements.
basis: section:Only Primitive Streams Have sum() and average(), and IntStream.sum() Overflows

aspects.says: IntStream.range excludes its end and rangeClosed includes it; an empty range is not an error.
basis: section:A Generated Sequence Ends Only Where Its Factory Says
aspects.reason: the transfer-stats practice grades an exclusive end through Arrays.stream(array, from, to); range itself is a one-call idiom

aspects.says: Pattern.splitAsStream takes a regular expression, keeps a leading empty piece and drops trailing ones.
basis: section:String.chars() Streams UTF-16 Units, Not Characters
aspects.reason: its rules are the regex engine's and the javadoc's; nothing in them is a stream decision a practice could grade
